versions.text: Verify the landing gear and engine inlet geometry are designed to prevent possible FOD to engines. DoD/MIL Doc: JSSG-2009 Appendix A: A.3.4.1.2.3/A.4.4.1.2.3 Ground FOD AFGS-87139: 3.2.1.1 General, 3.2.1.2 Arrangement; and 3.2.1.3 Clearances.

Criterion: Verify that the landing gear and engine inlet geometry are designed to prevent possible foreign object damage and excessive water ingestion into the engines. Standard: The location of the main and nose gear tires minimizes the throwing of debris, water, snow, and slush into the engine inlet, causing unacceptable degradation of engine performance. The design limits inlet exposure by establishing acceptable spray patterns and thrown object trajectories. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analyses and tests. Design analysis verifies compatibility of gear and inlet locations along with projected spray patterns for debris, water, snow and slush. Air vehicle ground tests verify that there is no excessive ingestion into the engines. References: JSSG-2009: A.3.4.1.2.3, A.4.4.1.2.3 Ground FOD AFGS-87139: 3.2.1.1 General; 3.2.1.2 Arrangement; 3.2.1.3 Clearances

Standard: The landing gear design limits engine inlet exposure by establishing acceptable spray patterns and thrown object trajectories. The location of the main and nose gear tires minimizes the throwing of debris, dirt, water, snow, and slush to prevent damage to the air vehicle and engines (e.g., loss of thrust, engine FOD ingestion, fuel tank rupture, and structural damage to flight-critical components). Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct a trajectory analysis to verify that the landing gear configuration does not direct runway contaminants (e.g., water and slush) or debris into the engines or damage the air vehicle. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
  (1) Conduct ground demonstration to verify that the landing gear configuration does not direct runway contaminants (e.g., water and slush) or debris into the engines or damage the air vehicle.
